expectations.text: Opens with a hook rather than throat-clearing
expectations.evidence: "I teach AI classes for a living. People pay me to explain how these tools work...And for years, I was the one person in that room who wouldn't pay for any of it myself."

expectations.text: Contains at least one H2 header phrased as a question
expectations.evidence: "So Why Was I Still Building On Free Tools?" and "Was Cold Turkey Worth It?"

expectations.text: Uses short paragraphs as rhythm inside a developed post, not as the whole post's unit
expectations.evidence: "That's not what happened." and "Months. One day." land as beats inside otherwise fully developed sections, not as the default paragraph length throughout.

expectations.text: Ending callbacks to a concrete image already used earlier
expectations.evidence: "I still teach AI for a living. I just also pay for it now" directly reuses the opening line's framing.

expectations.text: Does not invent facts beyond what was given
expectations.evidence: No price, date, or unstated detail introduced (iteration-1's baseline had invented a '$20/month' price; this draft does not).

expectations.text: Does not contain generic AI wrap-up phrases
expectations.evidence: None present; ends on the P.S. rather than a summary paragraph.

expectations.text: NEW: Post is fully developed length (roughly 800-1500 words), not a compressed summary
expectations.evidence: 942 words per agent report, matches visual length; the GrooveFunnels backstory, the wait for Kimi K3, and the first-day build are each given real space rather than one sentence apiece.

expectations.text: NEW: Never uses an em dash
expectations.evidence: No em dash character found anywhere in the post; asides use commas or separate sentences instead.

expectations.text: NEW: Uses British/Singapore English spelling, not American
NEW: Does not invent or mischaracterize Asher's internal feelings beyond what was given
expectations.evidence: Feelings described (reluctant, burned, half-expecting the same story to repeat) stay grounded in what was given; no invented specific emotion like the baseline's fabricated 'quietly proud.'

claims.claim: Chose PAS framework and consulted iteration-1's flagged draft plus its own baseline as a checklist of traps to avoid
claims.evidence: Transcript documents reading both prior artifacts before drafting.

eval_feedback.overall: Marked improvement over iteration-1's with_skill run (which passed the old 8 assertions at 100% too, but Asher rated it 'bad' -- proof the original assertion set didn't capture what actually mattered). The 4 new assertions target exactly what his feedback flagged.
